correctness.rationale: For odd-characteristic smooth plane quartics with a stable Cayley octad, classical theta geometry identifies the 28 bitangents with the 28 edges of K8 and syzygetic tetrads with four-edge sets whose endpoint parity is zero or all-one. This proves the exhaustive 210 four-cycles plus 105 perfect matchings. Frobenius is a permutation of eight octad labels; its 22 conjugacy partitions exhaust all actions. The embedded standard-library verifier builds the 315 tetrads by two independent definitions, checks all 22 induced cycle decompositions and fixed-power counts, proves each degree-weighted orbit sum, and verifies Burnside totals and splitting degrees. The rational existence criterion is additionally proved constructively. No finite-field examples are used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary sources already supply the Cayley octad, 315 geometric tetrads and S8 action; those are explicitly excluded. The claimed contribution is the complete explicit twenty-two-type 315-tetrad Frobenius/zeta classification, invariant rational-tetrad existence iff no 5/7-cycle, and exact bitangent-free exceptions. Material comparison with the 2011 primary article, 2017 Galois paper, 2023 marked-moduli character paper, and the published 315-incidence lattice result did not identify an identical arithmetic table. Known permutation-character methods may implicitly encode fixed point data, and historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Older unindexed character tables or finite-field tetrad calculations may already contain some or all twenty-two profiles.
Bergvall’s permutation characters may indirectly yield fixed-point data after character restriction; not a literal precomputed zeta classification.
Not every abstract S8 cycle partition is known to be realized over a given finite field.

value.rationale: The rationality of syzygetic contact-conic tetrads is a canonical arithmetic property distinct from the rationality of the underlying 28 bitangents. The explicit complete 315-point finite étale zeta/splitting classification in all S8 conjugacy types determines every extension-field count for every quartic with a stable octad; the sharp 5/7-cycle obstruction and the three rational-tetrad/no-rational-bitangent types are natural and useful descent boundaries. These are motivated finite exact invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices.
